messages.content: How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" They want to know how much gas is generated? But heating a closed chamber with air doesn't generate gas; it just increases pressure. Maybe they want to calculate the pressure increase? Or maybe they think gas expands? The question: "How much gas is generated from heating a 2 m³ closed chamber with air at a temperature of 25°C to 100°C?" That seems like a misunderstanding. We can interpret: They want to know the change in pressure or the amount of gas? The volume is fixed, so the amount of gas (moles) remains constant. So no gas is generated. The pressure will increase according to ideal gas law: P2 = P1 * T2/T1. T in Kelvin. So initial T=25°C=298K, final T=100°C=373K. So pressure ratio ~373/298=1.252. So pressure increases by ~25.2%. If initial pressure is 101325 Pa, final ~126,800 Pa. So no gas generated. So answer: no gas generated; pressure increases. Provide explanation. Also maybe compute moles: n = PV/RT. Use initial conditions: P=101325 Pa, V=2 m³, R=8.314 J/mol·K, T=298 K. n = (101325*2)/(8.314*298) ≈ (202650)/(2477.7) ≈ 81.8 mol. So same moles. So no gas generated. Provide answer.
